requirement: The system shall lock an account after five consecutive failed login attempts.

reference_scenarios.description: A user with 2 consecutive failed attempts is still allowed to log in.
A user with exactly 4 consecutive failed attempts is still allowed to log in (immediately below the limit).
A user with exactly 5 consecutive failed attempts is locked out (the stated threshold).

The attempt count is negative (e.g. -1), which cannot occur under normal use. The requirement does not define expected behavior for this case; it should either be rejected/validated or explicitly documented as always-allowed, rather than silently passing through as it does today.

The attempt count is a non-integer value (e.g. a string), which the current implementation does not guard against. The requirement implies a countable integer; invalid types should be rejected rather than causing an unhandled error.

notes: Source function has no input validation. neg_1 and edge_1 exist to surface that gap; they are reference-only cases the AI-generated scenarios should ideally also flag, since the requirement is silent on invalid input.
